offers_products.reason: Supplies medical products: diabetes supplies, sleep and respiratory equipment, wound care, urology and ostomy supplies delivered to patients' homes.

offers_services.reason: Apria provides home respiratory and sleep care, patient education and support services alongside equipment; also rentals.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Patients receiving care at home are the end users and recipients, though insurers often pay.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Connects with providers and insurers, which pay and refer; also government payers like Medicare.

recurring_revenue.reason: Ongoing resupply of diabetes, ostomy, urology and sleep supplies plus equipment rentals for chronic conditions.

cyclical_demand.reason: Chronic-condition home medical supplies and respiratory care are medically necessary and not easily postponed.

big_ticket.reason: Frequent small resupply orders and monthly rentals of medical supplies, not large infrequent purchases.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue comes mainly from medical products, equipment and delivery logistics rather than staff time and skill.

large_customers.reason: Main buyers are individual patients, with insurers and Medicare paying; not mainly large enterprise customers.

asset_heavy.reason: Needs rental equipment fleets, branches, distribution centers and delivery vehicles across the US.

notes: Judgment based on Apria and Byram home care businesses; the former Owens & Minor products business may be separate.
